- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to reflect risk-off bias.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, apply “lag correction”: reduce forecast by 5–10% in the next 2–3 periods.  
- If history shows mean reversion (e.g., recent prices trending down from peak), model often fails to revert; apply “mean reversion bias” by smoothing forecast toward recent 5–7-day average.  
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is volatile or mixed (±0.33), model tends to overfit short-term noise; dampen forecast volatility by 10–20% relative to historical std.  
- If model consistently forecasts higher than true outcome in early periods of a 30-day window, apply “early bias correction” — reduce first 5–7 forecast values by 2–5%.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.33 → -0.33 → +0.33), model often misreads momentum; apply “sentiment momentum filter” — reduce forecast if sentiment flips within 3 days.
